transcript:
Meeting header: POC Weekly Sync - Reliability Incident Follow-up
Date: 2026-03-27 15:00 PT | Duration: 45m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE); Liam O'Neal (Redwood SE); Sara Patel (VerdantHealth, Head of ML); Daniel Kim (Platform); Priya Rao (Security)

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining on short notice, um we'll keep to 45, we want to go through the incident recap and next steps
[00:18] Sara: thanks, yeah last week we saw a few user-facing failures; roughly 2pm PST on Thursday we had spikes of timeouts and a handful of 5xxs, roughly 20 minutes of elevated errors
[00:32] Daniel: the alerts were primarily for request timeouts at our edge gateway, some of them converted to 502 from the upstream redwood endpoint
[00:46] Liam: got it; we pulled the initial logs and we saw increased latency on token generation at about the same time, not full timeouts for all requests but a tail that spiked
[01:05] Priya: importantly for us, any logs we share need to be PII redacted and transferred via the secure S3 bucket, not email
[01:18] Maya: absolutely, we will upload to your shared bucket with a presigned link and mask payloads; Liam can you confirm what we'll include?
[01:28] Liam: yes we'll include request IDs, truncated request/response pairs (no PHI), stack traces from the serving runtime, and kernel/error traces where present
[01:38] Sara: thanks — I'll pull the request IDs for three representative failures and paste them into the ticket after the call
[01:47] Maya: perfect. quick question: were these requests coming from hosted or your dedicated infra?
[01:55] Daniel: this is the hosted POC setup hitting Redwood hosted endpoints; we are testing planned migration to a dedicated pool but that's not live yet
[02:06] Liam: ok that matters because hosted routing can hit capacity constraints; we saw a short period with elevated queue depth on some instances which can manifest as timeouts downstream
[02:20] Sara: also worth noting our client side uses synchronous blocking calls with no exponential backoff — we may be amplifying retries
[02:31] Maya: that's a useful signal. we'll recommend a client backoff pattern and a small change in SDK config — Liam do you want to propose numbers?
[02:39] Liam: recommend initial backoff 200ms, jittered, with exponential up to 2s, and max retries 3 for idempotent requests; for generation calls reduce to 2 retries to avoid token duplication
[02:54] Daniel: can you also send a snippet for our node SDK? our infra team prefers copy-paste
[03:00] Liam: yes will send code sample after the call
[03:06] [03:12] Maya: moving on to rate limits — we saw some 429s in the same window, which could be the edge rate limiter kicking in for some bursty clients
[03:23] Sara: we had a sudden product test that generated a burst; I think a test script started and created sudden concurrency
[03:31] Daniel: that was an internal QA run, forgot to toggle staging flag, sorry about that
[03:36] Priya: from security perspective we are fine, it's more an operational issue
[03:41] Liam: on our side we can surface per-API route rate limits and temporary burst allowances; for POC we can request a soft bump to the hosted quota while you run the burst test in a controlled manner
[03:55] Maya: we can also enable short-lived capacity bursts for the next run if you want — it's not infinite but will smooth peaks
[04:06] Sara: that would be helpful, yes; also we want to capture exact timing so we can correlate across services
[04:12] Maya: on correlation: please include the client timestamp and the Redwood request ID, that helps us match logs
[04:20] Daniel: noted
[04:25] [04:30] Liam: quick note on 5xxs — some were 502/504 which correlated with internal queue drain; a few looked like transient kernel failures in the runtime, we've flagged them for deeper analysis
[04:44] Sara: do you think this is model-level (long inference) or infra? we saw spikes on medium-length prompts too, not just long ones
[04:52] Liam: preliminary look suggests it was infra/queue related, not model OOMs; we saw CPU pressure on host process and queued requests timing out behind it
[05:04] Priya: please confirm any of that has no customer data exposure and is isolated
[05:10] Liam: confirmed isolation; no cross-tenant leaks and logs are scoped to your tenant id
[05:16] Maya: we'll include that statement in the security annex and the log upload
[05:20] [05:25] Sara: what's your recommendation for immediate mitigation? we had user impact and want to avoid recurrence during the pilot
[05:31] Liam: immediate: apply the backoff, reduce parallelism on the client, and ask Redwood to enable a temporary burst quota; medium-term: run dedicated staging benchmark with similar concurrency and token distribution to capture tail latency
[05:48] Maya: for the bench, we propose a 50k token run with your typical prompt mix; we can spin that in Dedicated staging which isolates variables
[05:58] Daniel: timeline? we have a maintenance window next week on Tuesday night, could that be used?
[06:04] Liam: yes we can provision staging Dedicated ahead of that maintenance, run tests during the window, and dump raw metrics for you
[06:12] Priya: on the staging run we'll need an NDA amendment? nothing major but want audit trail for tests
[06:19] Maya: we can add an amendment note; I'll loop in legal after the call
[06:25] Sara: earlier you mentioned kernel traces — do you have an ETA on root cause?
[06:32] Liam: we have an engineering thread; first pass root cause analysis looks like a combination of transient queue saturation plus an edge case in our memory reclaim path under burst load — we need deeper kernel-level traces to be sure
[06:48] Daniel: is that likely to recur on Dedicated?
[06:53] Liam: less likely on Dedicated because you get reserved capacity and less multi-tenant interference; still we want to run the benchmark to validate
[07:02] Maya: ok, let's recap the data exchange: Liam will upload sanitized logs to your S3 presigned folder, Sara will drop request IDs into the ticket, and Daniel will schedule the Dedicated staging run for the maintenance window
[07:17] Sara: yes I will add the IDs after the call
[07:21] [07:27] Maya: any blockers from security? Priya?
[07:30] Priya: main ask is redaction and for the link to expire after 7 days; also we need an attestation that logs don't contain PHI
[07:38] Liam: we'll include an attestation and set presigned links to 7 days; we'll also redact payload bodies by default
[07:46] Daniel: can you put the attestation text in the ticket so we can have it for audit?
[07:51] Maya: yes I'll paste the attestation and the planned artifact list
[07:56] [08:02] Sara: switching to observability — we want more granularity per model route, token-level latencies in the console if possible
[08:12] Maya: a roadmap item, but for pilot we can surface an adhoc dashboard and CSV export of per-request latencies
[08:20] Liam: I'll attach a sample CSV with the latency buckets and request metadata after the call
[08:27] Sara: that will help correlate with our APM
[08:30] [08:36] Daniel: one operational question — does enabling bursts affect billing? we want to understand cost impact during the test
[08:44] Maya: it does for hosted; we'll flag burst usage separately and estimate cost, but for pilot we can discuss a one-off credit if this was an experiment on our side
[08:56] Sara: appreciate that
[09:00] [09:12] Liam: quick note — SDK update: we saw some customers using naive retry loops which can cause thundering herd; we have an SDK patch that enforces jitter and sensible defaults, recommend you roll that in
[09:24] Sara: what version? we're on 1.4.2 currently
[09:29] Liam: patch will be 1.4.4; I'll include migration notes and a small changelog
[09:35] Maya: we'll send the PR and the sample config
[09:40] [09:48] Priya: will the SDK change require SSO reauth or any infra change?
[09:54] Liam: no SSO changes; purely client-side retry/backoff logic
[09:58] [10:05] Sara: ok next, the follow-up meeting — can we reconvene after you upload logs and we run the staging test? same time next week?
[10:14] Maya: yes propose 2026-04-03 same time, I'll send a calendar invite; if bench completes earlier we can do earlier
[10:22] Daniel: fine
[10:25] [10:31] Maya: any other questions?
[10:34] Sara: just one — are you seeing any persistent error patterns in the last 24 hours?
[10:38] Liam: no persistent issues post-mitigation; a couple of low-rate 5xxs but not correlated to high tail latencies; we'll monitor and alert you if we see a reoccurrence
[10:49] Priya: please include retention policy for logs we upload
[10:53] Maya: we'll keep them for 30 days by default, can extend on request
[10:58] [11:04] Maya: recap of owners and deliverables: Liam uploads logs and kernel traces (sanitized) by 2026-03-29; Sara posts request IDs by 2026-03-28; Daniel schedules staging run for maintenance window 2026-04-02; Maya sends pricing/attestation and SDK patch link by 2026-03-30
[11:25] Sara: thanks all
[11:28] Daniel: thanks
[11:30] Priya: thanks
[11:32] Maya: end meeting
